comparisons.peer_topic: Segment accounting policies and performance measures
comparisons.peer_summary: The reportable operating segments use the same accounting policies as disclosed in Note 1, and the Chief Operating Decision Maker uses Income (loss) from continuing operations as the primary performance measure for evaluating and allocating resources to segments.
comparisons.comparison: MS and C both disclose the role of the CODM in evaluating segment performance and allocating resources. MS states the CODM evaluates segment performance and allocates resources based on various financial considerations. C states the CODM uses Income (loss) from continuing operations to evaluate segment results and allocate resources. While the specific primary metric differs (MS lists multiple including pre-tax measures and return on equity, while C specifies Income from continuing operations), both disclosures confirm the CODM's active role in resource allocation based on specific segment profit measures.

sentences.text: The Firm's CODM is its Chief Executive Officer, who evaluates segment performance and allocates resources based on numerous business, strategic and financial considerations.
The segment profit measures are calculated in accordance with U.S. GAAP and are consistent with the amounts presented in the Firm's consolidated income statement.

The CODM uses Income (loss) from continuing operations as the performance measure, to evaluate the results of each reportable operating segment by comparing to and monitoring against budget and prior year results.

This information is used to allocate resources to each of the segments and to make operational decisions when managing the Company, such as whether to reinvest profits or to return capital to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases.

comparisons.peer_topic: Chief Operating Decision Maker and performance metrics
comparisons.peer_summary: The firm's president and chief operating officer serves as the chief operating decision maker (CODM), who allocates resources and assesses segment performance principally based on total net revenues, pre-tax earnings, net earnings applicable to common shareholders, and return on average common equity.
comparisons.comparison: Both MS and GS explicitly define the Chief Operating Decision Maker (CODM) and list 'return on average common equity' as a key metric for evaluating segment performance and allocating resources. MS states the CODM is the CEO and evaluates metrics including 'Return on average common equity' alongside income before taxes and pre-tax margin. GS identifies the CODM as the president and COO, who allocates resources based on metrics principally including 'return on average common equity', pre-tax earnings, and net revenues. While both use return on average common equity, MS also highlights pre-tax margin and income before taxes as primary financial considerations, whereas GS emphasizes total net revenues and pre-tax earnings.

sentences.text: The Firm's CODM is its Chief Executive Officer, who evaluates segment performance and allocates resources based on numerous business, strategic and financial considerations.
The CODM's financial considerations include analysis of multiple segment profit measures, such as Income before provision for income taxes and Pre-tax margin.
Furthermore, the CODM evaluates certain additional segment performance metrics including Return on average common equity.
The firm's chief operating decision maker (CODM) is its president and chief operating officer.

The CODM makes operating decisions, assesses the performance of, and allocates resources to, the firm's operating segments principally based on the total net revenues of the segments, revenues net of provision for credit losses, total operating expenses, pre-tax earnings, net earnings applicable to common shareholders and the return on average common equity to assess the performance of the segments.

comparisons.peer_topic: Operating Committee Review of Segment Performance
comparisons.peer_summary: The Operating Committee reviews segment results, including net interest income, noninterest revenue, noninterest expense, provision for credit losses, and net income on a managed basis. These measures are used to evaluate segment performance and make key operating decisions, such as resource and capital allocations.
comparisons.comparison: MS and JPM both describe a senior management body (CODM/Operating Committee) that evaluates segment performance and makes resource allocation decisions. MS identifies the CODM as the CEO who allocates resources based on segment profit measures. JPM describes the Operating Committee reviewing segment results (including net interest income, noninterest revenue, etc.) to make key operating decisions including resource and capital allocations. Both disclosures highlight the use of specific segment financial measures to drive strategic resource distribution.

sentences.text: The Firm's CODM is its Chief Executive Officer, who evaluates segment performance and allocates resources based on numerous business, strategic and financial considerations.
These measures are regularly provided to the CODM and are a component of a multifaceted decision-making process regarding segment performance as well as resource and capital allocation.
The Operating Committee reviews segment results including net interest income, noninterest revenue, noninterest expense, provision for credit losses and net income on a managed basis.
The Operating Committee uses these measures to evaluate segment performance and to make key operating decisions, including resource and capital allocations.
